title: Option Volatility and Pricing: Advanced Trading Strategies and Techniques (2nd ed.)
why: The options desk's standard text: volatility, Greeks, spreads and risk, explained without heavy maths.
caveats: US examples; India notes in the site's guide Greeks for a day trader. McGraw-Hill's own product page no longer resolves, hence the catalogue link.

title: Volatility Trading (2nd ed., + website)
why: How to measure, forecast and trade volatility, with position sizing (Kelly) and the psychology of being short gamma.
caveats: Wiley US prices; mathematical; US examples.

title: Positional Option Trading: An Advanced Guide
why: Where the edges in options actually come from (variance premium, skew, event vol) and how to harvest them with risk control.
caveats: Wiley US prices; assumes Volatility Trading; US data.

title: Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives (11th ed.)
why: The university reference for pricing, hedging and the mechanics behind every Greek the site's calculator shows.
caveats: Pearson US prices (Indian editions are cheaper); a textbook, not a trading manual.

title: Options Theory for Professional Trading (Varsity module 5, PDF)
why: Offline copy of the best free Indian options text; the same content as the Varsity module 5 course row.
caveats: Timeless concepts, pre-2024 rules (weekly expiries, lot sizes).

title: NISM Series-VIII Equity Derivatives — certification workbook
year: edition year printed on the cover (check at download)
why: The regulator-institute's own account of F&O products, margining, settlement and SEBI rules — free.
caveats: Behind a name/email/mobile form; dry; confirm the edition reflects the 2024–25 SEBI measures.

title: Trading Price Action Trends: Technical Analysis of Price Charts Bar by Bar for the Serious Trader
why: The densest treatment of intraday market structure (trends, pullbacks, breakouts) that the site's price-action guide draws on.
caveats: Wiley US prices; notoriously hard prose; US 5-minute E-mini charts.

title: Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard: How to Achieve Super Performance in Stocks in Any Market
why: Momentum stock selection (trend template, VCP) and strict risk rules from a US Investing Champion; the swing/positional complement to intraday setups.
caveats: US stocks; swing not intraday; no India notes.

title: Maximum Trading Gains with Anchored VWAP
why: The only full-length book on anchored VWAP, the tool behind the site's VWAP guide and the VWAP reclaim-and-reject playbook.
caveats: Self-published; US stocks; price varies by region.

title: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
by: John J. Murphy (New York Institute of Finance / Penguin)
why: The reference every TA course paraphrases: trends, patterns, indicators, intermarket analysis.
caveats: Timeless, pre-2024 rules; 1990s charts; treat pattern hit rates with the scepticism of the site's candlesticks and order-flow guide.

title: Mind Over Markets: Power Trading with Market Generated Information (updated ed.)
by: James F. Dalton, Eric T. Jones, Robert B. Dalton (Wiley)
why: The Market Profile / TPO text behind the site's volume profile guide.
caveats: Wiley US prices; CBOT futures examples; dense.

title: The Art and Science of Technical Analysis: Market Structure, Price Action, and Trading Strategies
why: Price action with statistics: which patterns have an edge, how to test them, and a complete trading plan.
caveats: Wiley US prices; US data.

title: Evidence-Based Technical Analysis: Applying the Scientific Method and Statistical Inference to Trading Signals
why: The antidote to indicator folklore: data-mining bias, hypothesis tests and why most published TA rules fail out of sample.
caveats: Wiley US prices; statistical; US S&P 500 tests.

title: How to Make Money Trading Derivatives: An Insider's Guide
why: The best-known Indian author on Nifty futures and options trading, written for NSE instruments and Indian sessions.
caveats: Timeless, pre-2024 rules — lot sizes, margins and expiries are long superseded; the author died in 2023; the publisher's site did not resolve, so the catalogue link is a Google Books ISBN record (whose author field is wrong).

title: Technical Analysis (Varsity module 2, PDF)
why: Offline copy of the free Indian TA module.
caveats: Indicator-centric; same caveat as the module 2 course row.

title: Reminiscences of a Stock Operator
why: Jesse Livermore's lessons on sitting tight, pyramiding and overtrading — a century old and still the most quoted trading book.
caveats: Public-domain text; pre-regulation US bucket shops; read for psychology, not mechanics.

title: Systematic Trading: A unique new method for designing trading and investing systems
why: Position sizing by volatility targeting, forecast scaling and honest expectations — the framework behind the site's systematic guides.
caveats: UK/US futures examples; price not displayed on the publisher page (varies).

title: Advanced Futures Trading Strategies
why: Thirty tested futures strategies with full backtests and code pointers — the most recent rigorous systematic-trading book.
caveats: Global futures universe; Indian index futures need the site's lot/margin facts; long.

title: The Art and Science of Trading
why: Carver's forthcoming book on what discretionary and systematic traders share; listed so the library stays current.
caveats: Forthcoming; shown unranked until published (out 1 Dec 2026, pre-order only; no reviews yet).

title: Quantitative Trading: How to Build Your Own Algorithmic Trading Business (2nd ed.)
why: A retail quant's practical path: data, backtesting pitfalls, execution and running it as a business, updated in 2021 with ML notes.
caveats: Wiley US prices; US data vendors and brokers — map to the site's broker-API comparison guide.

title: Advances in Financial Machine Learning
why: Why naive ML backtests lie (leakage, overlapping labels, multiple testing) and how to fix them — mandatory before trusting any ML signal.
caveats: Wiley US prices; heavy maths and Python.

title: Machine Learning for Algorithmic Trading (2nd ed.)
why: End-to-end Python workflow (data, features, models, backtests with Zipline/Backtrader) with a maintained GitHub repo.
caveats: Packt's own page blocks automated fetches, so the O'Reilly catalogue page is linked; US data sources; some libraries have aged.

title: Python for Finance: Mastering Data-Driven Finance (2nd ed.)
why: The standard pandas/NumPy-for-finance text: time series, backtesting vectorised strategies, options pricing in Python.
caveats: Python 3.6-era code; US data; pair with Quantra's free Python course for hands-on practice.

title: Tidy Finance with Python
by: Christoph Scheuch, Stefan Voigt, Patrick Weiss, Christoph Frey (Chapman & Hall/CRC; free online)
why: Reproducible empirical finance in Python: factor models, portfolio sorts, backtesting — the open-access bridge from courses to research.
caveats: US CRSP/Compustat data (needs WRDS for full replication); academic.

title: Trading in the Zone: Master the Market with Confidence, Discipline, and a Winning Attitude
why: The probabilistic mindset (think in samples of 20 trades, accept risk before entry) that every risk guide on the site assumes.
caveats: Repetitive; no numbers — pair with the Varsity risk module and the site's guide Expectancy and drawdown maths.

title: The Disciplined Trader: Developing Winning Attitudes
by: Mark Douglas (New York Institute of Finance)
why: Douglas's first, more analytical book on why traders self-sabotage and how to build mental discipline.
caveats: Dated examples; read Trading in the Zone first.

title: Market Wizards: Interviews with Top Traders (updated ed.)
why: Interviews that show how differently great traders trade and how identically they manage risk.
caveats: Wiley US prices; 1980s US context; survivorship bias — none of the methods is a template.

title: Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom (2nd ed.)
why: Origin of R-multiples, expectancy and position sizing as the real drivers of results — the maths behind the site's calculators.
caveats: US examples; some self-promotion; concepts timeless.

title: The Daily Trading Coach: 101 Lessons for Becoming Your Own Trading Psychologist
why: 101 short, actionable exercises (journaling, state control, review routines) from a trading-floor psychologist.
caveats: Wiley US prices; US discretionary context.

title: Memoirs of Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds
why: Tulipmania, the South Sea bubble and the Mississippi scheme — the original account of crowd behaviour in markets.
caveats: Victorian prose; only the financial chapters matter.

title: Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth: The Common Stock Investment Performance of Individual Investors
by: Brad M. Barber, Terrance Odean (Journal of Finance, 2000; author PDF)
why: The classic evidence that the most active retail accounts underperform by the cost of their turnover — the academic twin of SEBI's loss studies.
caveats: US discount-broker data from 1991–96; a journal article.

title: SEBI DEPA-II profitability study FY25–FY26, 20 Aug 2026
by: SEBI, Department of Economic and Policy Analysis (study, 20 Aug 2026)
why: The regulator's current numbers on how individual equity-derivatives traders fared in FY25 and FY26 — the study the site's home page and risk guides quote.
caveats: A fifteen-broker sample of individual traders; a 91-page PDF — read the summary pages first, then the site's guide What SEBI's loss studies say.

title: Analysis of Profit and Loss of Individual Traders dealing in Equity F&O Segment
why: The regulator's first study of individual F&O traders' outcomes (FY22 data) — the baseline that its FY25–FY26 study updates.
caveats: The first of SEBI's loss studies; its FY25–FY26 successor is listed separately, and the exact figures are in the site's guide What SEBI's loss studies say.

title: Risk Management & Trading Psychology (Varsity module 9, PDF)
why: Offline copy of the free Indian risk module.
caveats: Same content as the module 9 course row.

title: Let's Talk Money: You've Worked Hard for It, Now Make It Work for You
why: The clearest Indian money-management system (cash-flow accounts, insurance before investing, index funds) from a former Mint consulting editor.
caveats: Tax rates and product rules move; check against the site's verified facts register.

title: Let's Talk Mutual Funds: A Systematic, Smart Way to Make Them Work for You
why: Current (2023) guide to choosing, holding and exiting Indian mutual funds, including index funds and debt-fund tax after 2023.
caveats: Debt-fund taxation moved again under the 2025 Act; read with the site's guide Tax for investors.

title: Value Investing and Behavioral Finance: Insights into Indian Stock Market Realities
why: Behavioural finance applied to Indian investors by the founder of PPFAS — bubbles, IPO manias and contrarian buying with Indian cases.
caveats: Pre-2014 market examples; timeless lessons.

title: Coffee Can Investing: The Low-Risk Road to Stupendous Wealth
by: Saurabh Mukherjea, Rakshit Ranjan, Pranab Uniyal (Penguin Random House India)
why: A rules-based Indian quality filter (10-year revenue growth and ROCE) plus an honest allocation framework for salaried investors.
caveats: Author runs a PMS that sells the strategy; backtests are the author's own.

title: Bulls, Bears and Other Beasts: A Story of the Indian Stock Market
why: Narrative history of Dalal Street from Harshad Mehta to the 2000s — the context behind SEBI's rules and the traps the site's retail-traps guide describes.
caveats: Some chapters are dramatised; the 2021 fifth-anniversary edition adds the years since 2016, and the catalogue link uses that edition's ISBN.

title: NISM Series-XV Research Analyst — certification workbook
year: edition year printed on the cover (check at download)
why: Free, regulator-institute text on financial statements, valuation and the RA regulations — a structured fundamentals syllabus.
caveats: Lead form; exam-oriented.

title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing (10th anniversary ed.)
why: The case for low-cost index funds in 300 pages, by the man who invented them.
caveats: Wiley US prices; US funds; India notes in the site's index-funds guide.

title: The Intelligent Investor, Third Edition (updated with new commentary by Jason Zweig)
why: Graham's margin-of-safety text with Zweig's 2024 commentary on index funds, meme stocks and today's costs.
caveats: US examples; the HarperCollins US page blocks automated fetches, so the Google Books catalogue page is linked; long.

title: A Random Walk Down Wall Street (50th anniversary ed.)
why: Why most active strategies fail after costs, with the 2023 edition covering crypto, SPACs and factor funds.
caveats: US-centric; the life-cycle allocation tables assume US accounts.

title: The Psychology of Money: Timeless Lessons on Wealth, Greed, and Happiness
why: Twenty short essays on behaviour, compounding and 'enough' — the most readable antidote to over-trading.
caveats: No methods or numbers; US anecdotes.

title: Dual Momentum Investing: An Innovative Strategy for Higher Returns with Lower Risk
why: The absolute-plus-relative momentum rule (GEM) with its backtest — the source for the site's trend-rule guide.
caveats: US/global ETFs; backtest ends 2013; the author's research site blocks automated fetches, so the book is the link.

title: Meb Faber's free books (Global Asset Allocation and three others, PDF)
why: Author-released PDFs comparing famous allocation models (All-Weather, Permanent, Ivy) on one data set — the free way into the site's all-weather, momentum and trend-rules guide.
caveats: Lead form; US ETFs; the author manages funds that implement the ideas.

title: The Bogleheads' Guide to Investing (2nd ed.)
by: Taylor Larimore, Mel Lindauer, Michael LeBoeuf (Wiley)
why: The community's own step-by-step plan: emergency fund, asset allocation, index funds, rebalancing, behaviour.
caveats: Wiley US prices; US accounts (401k, IRA) — translate with the site's guide on investing abroad from India.

title: The Four Pillars of Investing, Second Edition: Lessons for Building a Winning Portfolio
why: Theory, history, psychology and business of investing in one 2023 update — the best single book for a long-term global allocation.
caveats: US-centric; some statistics are US-only.

title: If You Can: How Millennials Can Get Rich Slowly
why: A 16-page free plan (save 15%, three index funds, rebalance) with a reading list — the shortest complete investing education.
caveats: Hosted on etf.com, which blocks automated fetches but opens normally in a browser; US fund names.

title: The Little Book of Valuation: How to Value a Company, Pick a Stock, and Profit (updated ed.)
why: Intrinsic and relative valuation in 300 pages, revised in 2024; the companion to Damodaran's free valuation webcasts (in the courses list).
caveats: Wiley US prices; US examples.

title: Markets and Taxation (Varsity module 7, PDF)
why: Offline copy of the only free Indian trader-taxation primer.
caveats: Income-tax Act 1961 numbering; the 2025 Act applies from 1 Apr 2026 — section numbers and rates must come from the site's guide Tax for traders under the Income-tax Act 2025. Pre-2024 rules.
